SEC24A-01.note: Plural subject 'larvae' plus habitual present set by 'whenever ... drops' gives 'are'. The Latin-plural subject pulls toward singular 'is'/'was'; the tense clue is outside the four-word window.

SEC24A-02.note: Two decisions: verb agrees with plural 'pastures' (are), pronoun refers to singular 'the field vole' (it). 'grass' sits right before the blank and pulls to 'is'; 'them' tempts by matching pastures.

SEC24A-03.note: Head noun 'lining' is singular; present from 'if the burning returns'. 'esophagus and stomach' looks like a compound subject and draws 'are examined'.

SEC24A-04.note: 'Harvest after harvest' takes a singular verb; 'some sixty years ago' requires simple past, ruling out present perfect. The repeated noun reads as plural and draws 'were'.

SEC24A-05.note: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes 'have' and the plural possessive 'their'. 'its' tempts because 'its dwarfing rootstock' just used 'its'.

SEC24A-06.note: Ellipsis of 'has appeared' after the earlier 'have appeared': the auxiliary 'has' must be kept, singular for 'form'. 'does' is idiomatic in speech and the strongest pull; 'have' attracts via 'ragweed'/'weeds'. Note: 'too' only marks ellipsis, it does not settle the item.

SEC24A-07.note: 'whether the stored vaccines had warmed...' is an indirect question inside a declarative, so a period, not a question mark; C is a comma splice, D a fused sentence. The question mark is attractive because 'whether' feels interrogative.

SEC24A-08.note: A participial phrase modifying the whole clause takes a comma; no comma makes 'root' the one leaving channels, a colon needs an explanation not a result phrase, and D leaves a fragment. D is strikable as a capitalised participle fragment.

SEC24B-01.note: Elided verb is 'resist(s)', so the pro-verb 'do' is needed, plural for 'kinds'. 'sandstone' adjacent to the blank pulls to 'does not'; 'are not' tempts as a generic negative.

SEC24B-02.note: Singular 'rotor'; the parenthetical list is not part of the subject. Present from 'as two engineers watch'. The three-item list right before the blank draws 'are'.

SEC24B-03.note: Head noun 'measurements' is plural; present from 'unless the delay ... is removed'. 'summit'/'satellites' interveners; singular 'is' attracts via 'summit'.

SEC24B-04.note: Plural 'Samples'; past from 'until a supply ship reached'. 'core' adjacent to the blank draws 'was sealed'.

SEC24B-05.note: Verb agrees with singular 'housing' (shields); the protected things are the plural 'sensors' (them). Plural 'girders' in the opening clause tempts 'shield'.

SEC24B-06.note: 'migrated' after the interrupter needs perfect 'has', singular for 'dune'; 'was/were migrated' is a bad passive of an intransitive. 'beds' adjacent to the blank draws 'have'.

SEC24B-07.convention: Colon between two independent clauses is permitted when the second develops the first; here it is a sequel rather than an elaboration, so it is weak but arguable.
SEC24B-07.note: 'within a decade' opens the second independent clause, so a semicolon; A is a comma splice and B attaches 'within a decade' to 'crust' and leaves 'ferns had rooted' run on. B is attractive because 'cooled into a crust within a decade' parses locally. Marking exclusive since the colon is not an elaboration, but flag D.

SEC24B-08.note: Compound predicate with one subject ('welder ground ... and refilled'): no comma. 'and,' is never right and 'And refilled' is an obvious fragment, so only the comma-before-and option competes.
SEC24B-08.drop_reason: Two of three distractors ('and,' and the capitalised 'And refilled' fragment) die without parsing, leaving a two-way comma-or-not choice that is too thin for the hard route.

SEC24C-01.note: Indefinite pronoun 'Everything' is singular; past from 'if ... found'. 'shelves' adjacent draws 'were'; 'were' also tempts as a mock subjunctive, and the present 'list' in sentence 1 tempts 'is'.

SEC24C-02.note: Head noun 'practice' is singular; past from 'before the railway reached them'. 'cards' adjacent to the blank draws plural; present perfect clashes with the past time clause.

SEC24C-03.note: Plural 'screens'; past from 'when a new owner emptied'. The present 'lists' in the although-clause and singular 'inventory' tempt 'has been removed'.

SEC24C-04.note: Plural 'pigments' takes 'match' and the comparison pronoun must be plural 'those' (the pigments of the larger copies). 'copy' adjacent draws 'matches'; 'that' tempts as the familiar comparison word.

SEC24C-05.note: Plural 'tablets' takes 'are'; the possessor is the singular 'shrine' (its only record). 'their' tempts by matching 'tablets', and could be stretched to unnamed pilgrims, but no plural antecedent supports it.

SEC24C-06.note: Bare 'stop' in a direct question requires do-support, singular for 'tower'; 'is/are' would need 'stopping'. 'two rival river towns' and 'cathedrals' pull toward 'do'. The deciding verb is five words after the blank.

SEC24C-07.note: Introductory infinitive phrase is set off by a comma before the subject. 'the,' is garbled; C turns the infinitive phrase into a fragment; B is the only real competitor (garden-path 'transcribe the interviews the volunteers').
SEC24C-07.drop_reason: Easy: 'the,' is garbled and the period option is a plain fragment, so it reduces to a basic introductory-phrase comma well below module-2 hard difficulty.

SEC24C-08.note: With three translators, 'Ruiz' is restrictive (identifies which one), so no punctuation. Commas and paired dashes would imply a single translator; C mixes a comma and a dash and is strikable. The comma-pair appositive is the strongest pull.

tells: In every subject-verb item the noun printed immediately before the blank disagrees in number with the true head (A-01 aside): A-02 'grass', A-03 'stomach', B-01 'sandstone', B-02 list, B-03 'satellites', B-04 'core', B-06 'beds', C-01 'shelves', C-02 'cards', C-04 'copy'. A test-taker using 'pick the opposite number from the adjacent noun' gets these right without finding the subject.

In the number x tense grids (A-04, B-04, C-01, C-02, C-03) the present-perfect or present option never wins when a past time clause exists, and present perfect never wins in any 2x2 tense grid (A-04, C-02, C-03); B-06 'has' is the only perfect key.
Pronoun x verb 2x2 items: key always has the pronoun NOT matching the verb's number in A-02, B-05, C-05 (mixed referents) but matching in A-05, C-04, so no consistent shape tell there.
Weak option sets: B-08 ('and,' and 'And refilled' are never right) and C-07 ('the,' garbled) leave two live options; C-08 C mixes comma and dash.
Key letter spread across 24 items is balanced (A6 B6 C6 D6), no letter tell.

phase2_note: All 24 keys match my cold answers; every explanation's path produces the key and handles each distractor. SEC24B-07's explanation explicitly rejects the colon as non-elaborating, which settles my phase-1 flag. Batch-level concern stands: in 10 SVA items the noun adjacent to the blank always has the wrong number, so 'opposite of the adjacent noun' solves them without locating the subject.
